rejected.title: Protecting ancient sites
card: Ancient sites, such as temples, tombs and old cities, are clues to the past. Once damaged or lost, they cannot be replaced.
Threats

War can damage or destroy sites. Looting is the theft of objects from a site, which also removes clues about how people lived. Tourism can wear down sites through crowds and pollution. Climate, such as floods, storms and rising seas, can also harm them.
Conservation
means caring for a site so that it lasts. It can include repairing damage, controlling visitor numbers and guarding the site.
Heritage listing
means a site is officially recognised as important. A listing, such as World Heritage status, can bring attention, rules and support for protecting it.
rejected.remember: Sites face threats such as war, looting, tourism and climate. Conservation and heritage listing help to protect them.

a.q: Staff at an ancient temple set a daily limit on visitors and repair its cracked walls. What are they doing?
opts: Conserving the site by caring for it
Heritage listing the site as important
Looting the site by removing its objects
Harming the site through tourism
a.why: Limiting visitors and repairing damage are ways of caring for a site so it lasts, which is conservation. Heritage listing is tempting, but it means officially recognising a site as important, not the hands-on work of looking after it.
a.clue: Think about what the staff are physically doing to the temple.

b.q: Thieves dig up pottery and statues from an ancient town and sell them. Why does this harm what historians can learn?
opts: The objects are removed, along with clues about the town
The crowds of visitors wear down the old town paths
Rising seas flood the town and wash away its buildings
The town gets official recognition and new rules
b.why: This is looting, which removes objects and the clues about how people lived. Tourism also harms sites, but the thieves here dug up objects and took them away, which is not crowd damage.
b.clue: Which threat involves taking things from a site?

a.q: What is the main aim of conserving an ancient site?
opts: To care for it so that it lasts for the future
To make it easier for the most visitors to enter
To replace it with a modern copy of the site
To move its objects to a place far from the site
a.why: Conservation means caring for a site so that it lasts. Letting in the most visitors is tempting, but tourism can wear a site down, so conservation may limit visitor numbers.
a.clue: Think about what conservation is meant to do for people in the future.
